label: text
text: All the stronger counties won in the cricket matches which were completed yesterday and there were several away victories.

label: text
text: Although both Surrey and Yorkshire (the champions) won, the latter move into second place at the expense of the former on account of the system of reckoning. Lancashire remain in first place. Hants, Gloucester, Somerset and Derby each move up two places as the result of their wins.

label: text
text: Particularly pleasing is the century by Sutcliffe, the batsman who made so many centuries in Australia.

label: text
text: The full record of the week's games shows Brooklyn to have gone through without a defeat, having taken five straight, including three from the Phillies, who are now leading the second division, having been passed by both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati. We have already reported the improving position of the Pirates, who won four of their five games.

label: text
text: In the American League the Senators drew closer to the Athletics by taking both of their games with them. Washington was beaten twice by Detroit, however, which won four out of five games during the week, while the Athletics broke even with St. Louis and beat the Yankees in the one game played. The Athletics have now won 24 and lost 10 games, while the Senators have won 24 and lost 12.

label: paragraph_title
text: AS PRESIDENT.

label: text
text:
St. Petersburg, Fla., May 2.
Walter Hagen (of America), British open golf champion and holder of the unofficial world's

label: text
text: title, has signed a contract to remain as president of the Pasadena Golf and Country Club of this city and to play as a representative of the club for two years, beginning December 1, 1925.

label: text
text: Salary stipulated in the contract was $30,000 a year.

label: text
text: COMING HERE?

label: text
text: Walter Hagen, the American is contemplating a world tour with Joseph Kirkwood (Australia's leading golf professional). Hence his absence from Prestwick.

label: text
text: The plan is to visit China, Japan and South Africa and to be back in England for the 1926 championship.

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: NEW RULES.

label: paragraph_title
text: BASKETBALL ANNUAL MEETING.

label: text
text: FOUR CHANGES.

label: text
text: Four important changes in the playing regulations were made in the annual meeting of the joint board basketball rules committee, held last month at the University of Pennsylvania Club, New York. The body was made up of eighteen delegates, fourteen of which were present, representing the Young Men's Christian Association, Amateur Athletic Union and the National Collegiate Athletic Association.

label: text
text: The four changes effected by the convening body were as follows:—

label: text
text: 1. The elimination of rule requiring players attending a jump ball to keep one hand behind the back.

label: text
text: 2. Abolition of goal zones, two free throws being awarded to a player-fouled only when in the act of throwing for a goal from the floor.

label: text
text: 3. Edges of the backboard to be considered in bounds.

label: text
text: 4. Overtime periods for high schools and younger players reduced from five to three minutes each.

label: text
text: OFFICIAL'S SARCASM.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: BERLIN. Tune s

label: text
text: The Allies' note was an, unpleasant shock for Germany, according to an official spokesman, who said the Government regard ed the situation very pessimistically.

label: text
text: He added that the demands were mostly ridiculous and trivial. Doubtless some would be rejected.

label: text
text: The spokesman made a sarcastic reference to the Allies' demand for the abolition of policemen's steel helmets which were not a menace to the peace of Europe.

label: text
text: POINTED DEMANOS

label: text
text:
LONDON, June 5
The Allied disarmament note to Germany makes a detailed analysis of the situation in Germany via a vis every military clause of the peace treaty and specifies the thirteen points on which infractions have occurred.

label: text
text: The note demands inter alia (1) reduction of the police from 180,000 to 150,000, while the military character thereof must disappear; (2) the destruction and transformation of certain types of factories; (3) the reorganisation of the German High Command and General Staff which "is similar to before the war," and reduction of the administrative personnel; (4) rectification of the military organisation of the railway system; and (5) suppression of short term enrollment in the Relchswehr and the military activities of various assistions.

label: text
text: The note also formulates miscellaneous demands relating to the when to the in war material and war requisitions and the nature of coastal land fortifications.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHEUNG CHAU NOTES.

label: paragraph_title
text: Cheung Chau June 6.

label: text
text: To-day the finishing touches to the Wireless Telephone installation was completed and communication we understand is established with the Water Police outfit in Hongkong, so we are longer at the mercy of the storms which formerly damaged or broke the cable, or of raiders who might sever the shore lines.

label: text
text: A large tent has been erected next to the Electric Light, Power house; it will be used for Evangelistic meetings, for the benefit of the Chinese who may care to attend. The Rev. P. H. Anderson (who arrived with his family from Tung Shan, Canton) is in charge of the services, which are expected to be conducted for the next two weeks.

label: text
text: Several ladies and some children, who have been ordered out of Tung, Shan, by the American Consul, or account of anticipated fighting in this district have come to thine haven of refuge.

label: text
text:
In spite of the heavy rains with which we were favoured on the King's Birthday, quite a fatilla of launches (5) fully dressed, spansed some time in the outer bay, although the afternoon cleared up nicely, the visitors, on these boats departed fairly early. The rain storm had considerably cooled things down and also given the plantations and gardens a good soaking.
We have it on good authority the repairs to the pier will not be undertaken until after the Typhoon season. It remains to be seen the structure in its present damage state will survive if a severe storm should come along, we hope it will not thus be exed.
The Chenning China Sank fitted with new hollers and will be back on the run for about the weeks.
